decisions.executionNote: Holder is on the right, pens left. Start right wrist turn toward holder while retaining elbow-up continuity; left waits.
Move right hand to outside of holder, completing horizontal inward-facing orientation. Approach remains open and above grasp height.
Previous approach rejected with zero motion. Halve increments for smooth right-arm IK continuation.
Continue right-side approach toward upper holder wall, using small translation and yaw increments.
Outside approach was rejected. Use a diagonal inward/forward grasp to avoid the wrist singularity and excessive lateral reach.
Holder shifted on contact. Correct inward and forward to bracket its body, then close; retention and uprightness require visual confirmation.
Small vertical retention test of holder; keep closed and check whether body follows before reorienting.
Retention test showed empty fingers. Open and approach the holder's visible body farther forward and lower; avoid assuming the prior grasp succeeded.
Close around the visible holder body and lift gently inward. Check RGB for retention and holder axis before proceeding.
Fingers appear empty above the holder. Reopen and lower to its mid-body with a small rearward correction, rather than grasping above its rim.
Correct toward the holder visible at the right edge of the wrist view, then close and make a short retention test. Holder may be tilted.
Holder is still offset to one finger. Reopen, correct farther toward the wrist-view body center, lower slightly, and close.
Holder body now appears between fingers. Lift and bring slightly inward while maintaining closure to assess retention and axis.
Lift test shows no retention; holder remains lying on table. Switch to an overhead grasp, opening and raising while pitching the right fingers down.
Continue overhead orientation and align over the lying holder; maintain clearance until wrist view centers its body.
Replan from the executed prefix. Descend over the holder's body at fixed near-downward orientation, with small centering corrections.
Close the overhead grasp on the holder, then lift gently away from the table. Check that the holder remains between the jaws.
Holder appears retained in overhead grasp. Bring it inward and rotate its long axis toward vertical while keeping the right gripper closed.
Holder is visibly retained with opening up. Finish righting and move it to a central receiving position; begin left overhead approach to the nearest marker.
Keep upright holder stationary. Align the left fingers over the near marker's cap-side body and finish the downward grasp orientation.
Center the marker laterally in the left wrist view, descend to body height, and close; right maintains the upright holder.
Lift the centered marker with the left gripper closed and begin righting it tip-up. Maintain the holder upright in the right hand.
Marker is visibly retained. Finish rotating it upright and carry it above the holder's near-left side with bottom clearance.
Align marker's lower end over the holder opening, adding clearance and correcting its remaining lean before insertion.
Lower the retained marker toward the opening with a small leftward/forward centering correction; keep the holder fixed.
Marker bottom is aligned above the opening. Lower slowly into the upright holder without releasing yet.
Seat the first marker farther into the opening, release it, and withdraw left/up while the right hand stabilizes the holder.
First marker remains in holder after release. Withdraw left and turn toward an overhead grasp of the remaining purple marker.
Replan after the one-step prefix; use half-size rotations and smaller translations to preserve left-arm joint continuity on the next approach.
Move left toward the second marker and continue pitching down, staying above its body while keeping the filled holder steady.
Finish the left overhead orientation while moving laterally over the remaining purple marker, leaving a small vertical margin for visual centering.
Center and align the second marker in the left jaws, lower slightly to its body, then close. Keep the holder stationary and closed.
Lift the second marker away from the table and start turning it upright while moving back from full reach. Check retention in RGB.
Second marker retained. Raise and rotate toward an upright insertion orientation while approaching the holder from the left.
Finish righting the second marker and align above the unoccupied side of the holder with vertical clearance.
Lower the second marker toward the empty right side of the opening; retain both grasps until its bottom is inside.
Seat and release the second marker beside the first, then withdraw the left fingers upward and left without disturbing the holder.
Second marker is leaning at the rim after release. Clear the left fingers slowly and let it settle; verify insertion before the next pickup.
Approach the yellow-trimmed pen from above with the left arm. The second marker's final seating is occluded and will need verification.
Continue overhead approach to the yellow pen. Wrist view now reveals the second purple marker on the table; it will require recovery.
Finish downward orientation and approach the yellow pen's central body; use wrist feedback before closure.
Align the yellow pen's long axis, move the pinch toward its upper body, lower and close while keeping the holder fixed.
Lift away from table contact while maintaining closure, then begin righting the yellow pen. Verify retention visually.
Yellow pen stayed on table. Reopen and return overhead, correcting toward its thicker upper body and slightly right before a deeper grasp.
Replan from the interrupted prefix: keep the near-vertical orientation, center the yellow pen leftward, descend gently, and close.
Hold closure briefly, then lift the yellow pen back and up at fixed wrist orientation to check retention without twisting it.
Yellow pen is visibly retained. Raise and draw it back while rotating its cap upward, leaving clearance above the holder.
Finish bringing the yellow pen upright above the holder, with bottom clearance. Keep both grasps closed.
Align the yellow pen bottom with the free portion of the opening and lower gradually, holding both objects securely.
Lower the yellow pen deeper past the rim before release; monitor for contact or displacement of the holder.
Release the yellow pen after its bottom passed the rim, pause for settling, then clear left/up without moving the holder.
Yellow pen remains seated after release. Clear the holder and start a cap-aligned overhead approach to the black pen with the left arm.
Continue toward the black pen, gradually pitching the left fingers downward and keeping clearance over the table.
Finish aligning the downward left fingers with the black pen's upper body, using gradual forward motion and descent.
Replan from the nine-step prefix. Keep the near-downward orientation fixed, descend slowly and center the black pen instead of extending farther.
Center the black shaft between the left fingers and close at table-level grasp height, keeping the holder stationary.
Lift back from table contact with the black pen centered and closure maintained; verify retention before rotating.
Black pen did not follow the lift. Reopen and shift toward its central upper shaft rather than the thin tip, descending for another grasp.
Fine-center the black shaft, lower to pinch height, close, and begin a small lift to test retention.
Allow the black-pen pinch to settle, then lift back at fixed orientation to verify that the pen follows.
Black pen follows the lift. Rotate it upright while raising and backing off from maximum reach; right hand keeps the holder steady.
Finish turning the black pen upright and position it over the holder with clearance before lowering.
Lower the black pen toward the opening with a small centering correction, keeping it held until its lower end is safely inside.
Guide the black pen deeper into the free side of the opening, reducing its lean slightly and maintaining both grasps.
Black tip is contacting the purple marker rather than clear space. Shift toward the visible free side, then resume a slow descent.
Black tip is now in the visible free portion of the opening. Lower farther past the rim, release, and pause to observe settling.
Withdraw the open left fingers from the holder to remove contact and inspect whether the released black pen settles inside.
Holder appears to have slipped and pens are moving. Clear both open hands without crossing and allow objects to settle before recovery.
Two pens remain in the upright holder on the table. Reapproach its side with the right hand while moving the left above the fallen black pen.
Align right fingers at the holder's mid-body from the side. Left continues its overhead approach to the black pen, with both grippers open.
Center and close the right grasp on the holder at table level; finish left downward alignment over the black pen's upper shaft.
Right grasp was empty and pushed the holder left. Reopen, raise to its mid-body, and realign. Left closes on the black shaft and tests a vertical lift.
Black pen is retained. Raise and turn it upright; fine-center the right jaws on the holder body and close without lifting yet.
Right fingers closed before reaching the holder. Reopen and advance to its mid-body; keep the black pen raised and finish turning it upright.
Pause the left arm after the continuity interruption. Close the centered right grasp and test a short vertical holder lift before insertion.
Holder follows the right lift. Align the black pen farther forward over its opening while keeping its tip above the rim; maintain both grasps.
Lower the upright black pen toward the near-center opening, keeping the holder fixed and watching for rim or pen contact.
Continue seating the black pen past the rim at fixed alignment; retain both grasps and check for holder displacement.
